# Graphics3D

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [Display](Blitz3D-Display)

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D width%, height%, depth%=0, mode%=0
```

**Works in:** Blitz3D

Opens the window, or full screen mode, that 3D programs are drawn in. It has to be the first graphics command of a 3D program: every other 3D command fails until it ran. After it, the back buffer is the target of drawing and you draw one frame at a time with [RenderWorld](RenderWorld) and [Flip](Flip).

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| 0 | Window while testing and full screen otherwise. This is the default. |
| 1 | Full screen. |
| 2 | Window. |
| 3 | Window whose size can be changed by the user; the picture is scaled to fit. |
| 4 | Window without a border: no title bar and no frame. This is a BlitzLLVM extension that original Blitz does not have. |

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 640, 480, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
camera = CreateCamera()
cube = CreateCube()
PositionEntity cube, 0, 0, 5

While Not KeyHit(1)
	TurnEntity cube, 1, 2, 0
	RenderWorld
	Flip
Wend
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | Int | required | Width of the picture in pixels. |
| `height` | Int | required | Height of the picture in pixels. |
| `depth` | Int | `0` | Color depth: 0 for the best, or 16, 24 or 32. Defaults to 0. |
| `mode` | Int | `0` | Window or full screen as in the table. Defaults to 0. |

**Differences and known gaps:**

* The depth is not used: pictures always have 32 bits per pixel, however much you ask for.
* A window without a border (mode 4) has the size you ask for and cannot be resized by the user.
